out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. OBSERVED EMPLOYEE CHANGING GLOVES AFTER HANDLING RAW MEAT WITHOUT WASHING HANDS.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO REMOVE GLOVES AND WASH HANDS BEFORE DONNING CLEAN GLOVES. PLEASE ENSURE EMPLOYEE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed the handsink at the END OF 3 COMPARTMENT SINK being used TO STORE UTENSILS.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EMPLOYEE REMOVED UTENSILS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: SPINACH, LAMB STEW AND LAMB SHANK ALL PREPARED FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: CHICKPEAS AT 54-60 FOR 5.5 HOURS IN DEEP COVERED PANS IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO TRANSFER TO FREEZER FOR RAPID COOLING TO 41F OR BELOW. PLEASE ENSURE TO USE SHALLOW PANS IN FREEZER , STIRRING FREQUENTLY TO RAPIDLY COOL FOODS. DO NOT COVER FOODS UNTIL COOLED TO 41F OR BELOW.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' OBSERVED NO SIGNED COPIES OF EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY ON SITE AT TIME OF INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS WILL EMAIL COPY TO PIC. PLEASE REVIEW WITH EMPLOYEES AND HAVE EACH SIGN A COPY. MAINTAIN SIGNED COPIES ON SITE FOR REVIEW BY THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: RAW CHICKEN OVER RAW BEEF IN TRUE 1 DOOR UPRIGHT REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC REORGANIZED DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE. K KABOB IN CHANTILLY (Inspection Date: 11/10/2025) Page 2 of 4

These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EDUCATION PROVIDED. COMPLIANCE WILL BE CONFIRMED BY FOLLOW UP INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Storage of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. OBSERVED QUATERNARY AMMONIA SANITIZER ON SHELVING ABOVE 3 COMPARTMENT SINK; CLEANING CHEMICALS ON SHELVING UNIT IN DRY STORAGE AREA WITH DRY GOODS, AND IN FRONT SERVICE AREA WITH SINGLE SERVICE ITEMS.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored below food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items to prevent contamination. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DESIGNATE STORAGE AREA FOR CHEMICALS AND KEEP ALL CHEMICALS AWAY FROM FOODS, EQUIPMENT OR FOOD SERVICE ITEMS.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: COOKED LAMB AT 56F IN COVERED PAN IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCARD FOOD DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE USE SMALLER PORTIONS, SHALLOW UNCOVERED PANS TO ENSURE FOODS ARE COOLED TO 135F TO 70F IN 2 HOURS AND TO A FURS 41 WITHIN A TOTAL OF 6 HOURS. DO NOT LEAVE COOKED FOODS OUT OF REFRIGERATION OVERNIGHT.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: 1) SQUEEZE BOTTLES OF SAUCES, 2) BULK CONTAINERS OF FOODS LIKE SALT, SUGAR, ETC.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO LABEL ALL WORKING CONTAINERS AND BOTTLES OF FOODS BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP. violations.observation: The food on display is not protected from contamination. Observed dessert type items not protected at the cashier station with a sneeze guard.
violations.corrective_action: Food on display shall be protected from contamination by the use of packaging, counter, service line, or salad bar food guards, display cases, or other effective means. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO MOVE THE DESSERT ITEMS TO THE NON-WORKING REFRIGERATOR AND ONLY SET OUT ONE OR TWO PIECES OF THE DESSERT AS “DISPLAY ONLY” UNLESS SNEEZE GUARDS ARE PROVIDED.

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. OBSERVED BUCKETS OF TZATZIKI SAUCE STORE DIRECTLY ON FLOOR IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR; FOODSTUFF STORED ON FLOOR IN DRY STORAGE AREA; FOOD DIRECTLY STORED ON THE FLOOR IN THE KITCHEN AREAS.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE ENSURE FOODS ARE STORED ON APPROVED SHELVING OR DUNNAGE RACKS BY FOLLOW UP INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Personal cleanliness

violations.title: Jewelry
violations.observation: Employees observed wearing jewelry on their arms and hands while preparing food.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall limit their jewelry to a plain wedding ring while preparing food. Food employees may not wear bracelets, watches, etc. because they can inhibit proper hand washing. PLEASE ENSURE JEWELRY IS REMOVED FORM HANDS AND ARMS WHEN PREPARING FOODS.

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. PLEASE ENSURE ALL KITCHEN STAFF INVOLVED IN FOOD PREPARATION ARE PROVIDED WITH HAIR COVERS.

EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE ENSURE SANITIZER SOLUTION OF BLEACH AT 50-200PPM IS PREPARED DAILY AND REFRESHED AT LEAST EVERY 4 HOURS. KEEP WET WIPING CLOTHS IN SANITIZER SOLUTION ONCE NOT IN USE.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS PROVIDED DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE REVIEW ALONG WITH EMPLOYEES AND MAINTAIN AT PREMISES FOR USE WHEN REQUIRED.

OBSERVED EMPLOYEE WITH GLOVES INVOLVED IN FOOD PREPARATION, CLEANING AND RETURNING TO PREPARE FOODS WITHOUT REMOVING GLOVES OR WASHNG HANDS.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS PROVIDED EDUCATION ON CHANGING GLOVES AND WASHING HANDS BEFORE RETURNING TO FOOD PREPARATION. EMPLOYEE REMOVED GLOVES AND WASHED HANDS DURING INSPECTION.

violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. PIC TRANSFER TO WALK IN UNIT DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE. READY TO EAT FOODS MUST BE STORED ABOVE RAW ANIMAL FOODS IN REFRIGERATOR.
